newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - July 30.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- The ruling New Korea Party's newly elected presidential candidate is continuously attacked by opposition lawmakers in parliament causing the passage of many pieces of legislation to be delayed.

- Pohang Iron and Steel Co and Dongkuk Steel Mill has proposed to buy Hanbo Steel Co's fixed assets only at two trillion won, but Hanbo creditors say the fixed assets are worth more than four trillion won.

- Prime Minister Koh Kun, instructed the Office of Military Manpower Administration to present the physical exam records of the two sons of ruling party presidential candidate Lee Hoi-chang to parliament as requested by opposition law-makers.
- Kia Group's creditors said they would provide 100 billion won to Kia Motors and Asia Motors if the group's current management gives up its rights.

- Jinro Ltd., the flagship of the troubled brewery giant Jinro Group, narrowly tided over the danger of going bankrupt on Tuesday as a local leasing company agreed to postpone its collection of Jinro-issued promissory notes.
